content: Administer 5 grams of the medication intravenously every 6 hours, or alternatively, administer Ampicillin-Sulbactam at a dose of 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours. Another option is to administer Clindamycin at a dose of 600 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours. For immunocompromised patients, the preferred regimen includes the following options: Administer Cefotaxime at a dose of 2 grams intravenously every 6 hours. Alternatively, administer Ceftizoxime at a dose of 4 grams intravenously every 8 hours. Another option is Piperacillin at a dose of 3 grams intravenously every 4 hours. Imipenem can also be administered at a dose of 500 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours. Alternatively, Gatifloxacin can be administered at a dose of 400 milligrams intravenously every 24 hours. These recommendations are supported by references from authoritative sources, including: Flint, Paul (2010). Cummings Otolaryngology: Head & Neck Surgery. Philadelphia, PA: Mosby/Elsevier. Thompson, Jerome W. (June 2008). Deep Neck Infection. Otolaryngologic Clinics of North America, 41(3): 459–483. PMID: 18435993. Hall, Jesse (2015). Principles of Critical Care. New York: McGraw-Hill Education. ISBN: 978-0071738811.
